subject: SDK toggle policy and back-compat windows
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@forgeworks.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: integrations@forgeworks.io
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SDK compatibility window + toggle policy for upcoming breaking API change

Hi Vanessa / Jordan,

We recently ran into a compatibility issue when Redwood changed a small field name in the v2 inference response last quarter. It caused a high-severity incident for several of our customers and pushed us to release a hotfix. ForgeWorks is actively building on top of Redwood's SDKs and we need better guardrails for future breaking changes.

Could we get alignment on two items for the next 6–12 months of roadmap changes: 1) a minimum compatibility window (our ask: 6 months for any breaking change to public SDKs/APIs), and 2) a formal toggle/feature-flag policy that allows partners to opt into experimental API behavior before we flip defaults.

I've attached a spreadsheet (forge_sdk_changes.xlsx) with the most recent surface area and a short impact matrix. Procurement is asking us to get these in writing as part of our renewal / expansion conversation.

Can we set a short call this week to scope what's feasible?

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Integrations, ForgeWorks
ellen@forgeworks.io

[Attachment: forge_sdk_changes.xlsx (spreadsheet, 56KB)]

Subject: Re: Request: SDK compatibility window + toggle policy for upcoming breaking API change

Thanks for flagging — reviewed the ForgeWorks matrix. A few product constraints and a proposed policy below: 

1) Compatibility windows
- Proposal: default 90-day compatibility window for minor, non-breaking SDK updates; 180-day window for breaking API changes that affect public surface area (what they see in SDKs). We can extend to 6 months in documented cases with a signed mutual action plan (MAP).

2) Toggle / opt-in policy
- For any change that is potentially breaking, we will provide: 
  - a feature-flagged preview endpoint (or SDK flag) available to partners for testing for at least 60 days, and 
  - a migration guide and automated linting checks in the SDK where feasible.

3) Versioning semantics
- Keep semantic versioning on SDKs: patch=bugfix, minor=add non-breaking features, major=breaking. Breaking change releases must be accompanied by an announced deprecation schedule and feature-flag preview.

Open questions for Eng (Jonas): effort to maintain preview endpoints / toggles (approx SRE + dev effort), and whether we can guarantee the 60-day preview for every platform change. Jordan/Vanessa: if ForgeWorks needs 6 months as a hard requirement, we may need a commercial commitment (e.g., extended support) — feel free to surface that in the call.

I drafted a short toggles policy doc (toggle_policy_draft.md) with examples — attaching.

—Karthik
Group PM, Redwood Console

[Attachment: toggle_policy_draft.md]

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SDK compatibility window + toggle policy for upcoming breaking API change

Quick eng notes / estimate after looking at the matrix: 

- Preview endpoints: medium effort (3–4 engineer-weeks total across runtime and SDK maintainers) to implement and maintain per major change. This includes a lightweight flag routing layer and temporary compatibility adapters in the runtime for back-compat.
- Back-compat maintenance cost: ongoing; we'd prefer 90–180 days by default and a documented extension process for special partners.
- Suggested policy text (draft):
  - "For Partner Preview: Redwood will provide a feature-flagged preview for any breaking change with a minimum 60-day testing window. After the preview period, Redwood will provide a 90-day production compatibility window before deprecated behavior is removed. Partners requiring longer windows can request an extended compatibility agreement with Redwood Support."

Attachment: I put an initial policy draft in toggle_policy_draft.md and a short timeline diagram in FW-compatibility-proposal.pdf. If we commit to 6 months for ForgeWorks specifically, we need to allocate a partial ongoing support SKU or acceptance that some preview endpoints will be maintained longer than the default.

Jonas
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Request: SDK compatibility window + toggle policy for upcoming breaking API change

Hi Ellen — thanks again for the clear ask and for the spreadsheet. Quick summary of where we landed internally and the proposal we'd like to present to ForgeWorks: 

- Default compatibility window: 90 days post-preview for production removal (180 days for explicitly documented breaking changes).
- Preview phase: 60-day opt-in feature-flagged preview available to partners.
- Extensions: Partners can request a 6-month compatibility contract; this would be tied to an extended-support add-on or an expansion commitment.
- Versioning: SDKs will follow semver; breaking changes require an announced deprecation and preview.

Attachments: toggle_policy_draft.md, FW-compatibility-proposal.pdf. Also shared a short doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy-toggle-policy-draft for collaborative comments.

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call Wednesday 11/25 10:00am PT? If that works, Jordan will send a calendar invite and we'll bring the policy draft and timeline.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
